passages.title: BC Greens focus on renters and childcare as NDP and Conservatives roll out economic plans (Victoria Buzz)
passages.quote: September 29th, 2026 By Mike Kelly (Doug Clement Photography) Share Facebook X ReddIt Email Copy URL BC’s provincial election campaign is picking up pace, with the province’s three major parties rolling out a series of new commitments on housing, childcare, resource development, energy and taxes. The BC Greens have focused much of their latest campaign push on affordability, announcing new plans aimed at renters and families while also drawing a clear line between themselves and the NDP and Conservatives on liquefied natural gas (LNG) development.

passages.title: BC Greens 2026: Our Plan for British Columbia (platform)
passages.quote: Implement a windfall tax on mega-corporation to bring in British Columbians fair share and build our revenue base to pay for community health centres, transit, and reign in the provincial debt. Create a fair royalty deal for oil and gas. We will eliminate the subsidies fossil fuel companies receive, regain control over royalty rates, and ensure existing LNG projects cover their own power costs instead of leaning on the public system. Deliver stronger public returns from B.C.'s natural resources, with community and Indigenous ownership.

passages.quote: — “I’m deeply disappointed to see LNG Canada Phase 2 move ahead with the Final Investment Decision—and to see both the BC NDP, Conservatives all applaud this move, while committing to further expansion of oil and gas throughout our province.
